deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's axiomatic 'tame' (modéré) spaces, with axioms labelled M1, MF, M11 earlier in the notes. This is an early version of what became o-minimal structures (van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn).

Data. X is a tame space and Y ⊂ X a tame subset. By the previous page, after replacing f_α by f_α − e_α, Y is the common zero set of tame real functions f_α, α∈I. The tame functions (g_β)_{β∈J} give an embedding X ⊂ R^J, so they separate the points of X.

Claim. The family {f_α} ∪ {f_α·g_β} vanishes on Y, still defines Y as its common zero set, and separates the points of X∖Y.

Proof as on the page. Take x ≠ y in X∖Y.
- Choose β with g_β(x) ≠ g_β(y); this exists because the g_β embed X.
- Choose α with λ = f_α(x) ≠ 0; this exists because x ∉ Y.
- If f_α(y) ≠ f_α(x), then f_α already separates x and y.
- Otherwise f_α(y) = λ ≠ 0, and then f_αg_β(x) = λg_β(x) ≠ λg_β(y) = f_αg_β(y).

Conclusion (Proposition, assuming M1, MF, M11). Suppose a tame Y ⊂ X is the common zero set of a finite family of tame functions. Then one can choose such a finite family that also separates the points of X∖Y. The finite version uses finitely many f's and the finitely many coordinates g_1..g_n of an embedding X ⊂ R^n.

What it serves. The map Φ = (f_α, f_αg_β) : X → R^N sends Y to 0 and is injective on X∖Y. So Φ realises the collapse X/Y set-theoretically as a tame subset of R^N. The closing parenthesis, '(lorsque X/Y est un espace modéré)', shows Grothendieck is using this to construct the quotient X/Y in the tame category, or to decide when it exists.

In modern terms this is the standard trick x ↦ (f(x), f(x)·x), with f a definable function whose zero set is Y (for instance the distance to Y). It is used to collapse a closed definable set to a point in o-minimal and semialgebraic topology.

The next page moves on to generic local triviality of tame maps and of finite diagrams (Hardt-type triviality).
errors: The proposition says the family 'sépare les pts de X'. It can only separate the points of X∖Y, since all of Y goes to 0. The text before the proposition says X∖Y correctly.

Topology is not addressed. Φ is a continuous injection of X/Y, but it need not be a homeomorphism onto its image for the quotient topology. If Y is non-compact, the quotient X/Y may not even be first countable or metrizable (e.g. collapsing a line in R^2). Grothendieck's parenthetical restriction '(lorsque X/Y est un espace modéré)' seems to acknowledge this, but the condition is not analysed.
Y has to be closed for the quotient to be reasonable. The word 'fermée' was struck out and replaced by 'modérée', yet a zero set of continuous functions is automatically closed.
Minor: the case split 'if the f_α do not suffice to separate x and y' is handled correctly. One needs f_α(y) = f_α(x), and the page gets this right.

ideas.what: Making a family of functions that cuts out Y also separate the points of X∖Y, by adjoining the products f_α·g_β with the coordinate functions of an embedding. This realises the collapse X/Y inside an affine space.
ideas.modern_name: Collapsing a closed definable subset to a point via x ↦ (f(x), f(x)x); existence of definable quotients X/Y
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in semialgebraic and o-minimal geometry: Delfs–Knebusch for semialgebraic spaces (1980s); van den Dries, 'Tame topology and o-minimal structures' (1998), ch. 10 on definable quotients
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6, only calls in general terms for a tame topology in which quotients such as X/Y exist. This specific trick is not published there.

ideas.what: Axiomatic tame-space framework with axioms M1, MF, M11 and modéré subsets defined by zero sets of tame functions.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches the programme; the M-axioms themselves seem unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine algebraic trick, the standard device for collapsing a closed definable set to a point, and it is well known in semialgebraic and o-minimal topology. The only historical interest is that it documents Grothendieck working out quotient constructions in his axiomatic tame topology before o-minimality existed. That fact is already known in outline from the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: 'définissant Y comme l'un des zéros communs' should read 'définissant Y comme l'ens. des zéros communs'.
The proposition likewise reads 'qui est l'ens. des zéros communs', not 'une des zéros communs'.
First line (struck): 'Si x ∈ X∖Y, ∃α tel que f_α(x) ≠ 0, ...'. The struck word after 'communs.' looks like 'de X', followed by ': on prouve [?], de plus elles séparent les pts de X∖Y'.
'on a M1' before '∃β' is uncertain in the image; it may read 'en effet'.
'f_α(y) (= f_α(x) = λ par hyp.) ≠ 0': the 'par hyp' (meaning 'par hypothèse', in the case where f_α does not separate x and y) is consistent with the image.
In the proposition, 'partie [-fermée-] {+modérée+} Y': the struck word is likely 'fermée', with 'modérée' inserted above. The machine transcription is plausible.
